clue.text: See 10
One of 4's, big interior, Japan hasn't an alternative

definitions.note: 4 is Norman Foster, so this means a building he designed

indicators.note: an alternative version of the letters is a reworked arrangement of them
Japan that has not got 'an' loses those two letters

explanation.surface: A traveller describes something vast inside, and Japan apparently offering no other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't an' strips AN from Japan, leaving JAP; BIG, INTERIOR and JAP are then rearranged ('alternative') into the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Foster and Partners designed the huge terminal at Beijing Capital, one of the architect's best-known projects.

clue.text: Model one piece of wood

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
deal is a plank of fir or pine timber

explanation.surface: A carpenter's exemplar: a single plank held up as the pattern to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A model as an adjective (a model pupil) is a perfect example, a synonym of flawless or exemplary.

clue.text: Short piece on metre-high eucalyptus

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes before it
a short word is cut off before its end, losing the final letter

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun

indicators.note: high in the sense of intoxicated, so the letters of metre reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A brief article about a eucalyptus that stands only a metre tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like part of the tree's height but signals an anagram of METRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalyptus trees are commonly called gums in Australia, from the sticky resin they exude.

clue.text: See 26
Old and new, very powerfully unique

parts.note: neo- is the prefix meaning new
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Something both ancient and modern, delivered with great force, is said to be like nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off is something made or happening only once, hence singular or without equal.

clue.text: Spicy quality in North African stews, including last of cumin and a dash of saffron

indicators.note: the stews take the other letters inside them

parts.note: tagines are slow-cooked Moroccan stews named after their pot

indicators.note: the final letter of the word cumin
just a dash, the opening letter of saffron

explanation.surface: A cookery note: tagines get their kick from cumin and saffron.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters go in separately: N after TA, S before the final S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanginess is a sharp, piquant flavour, the property of being zesty or spicy.

clue.text: Money problems, no capital

indicators.note: without its capital, the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: troubles are problems or difficulties

explanation.surface: Financial worries, compounded by having no capital to fall back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks financial, but means the first letter of TROUBLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Roubles are the Russian currency, so they are an example of money.

clue.text: Leave soon with English liberal and moderate

indicators.note: liberal in the sense of free and loose, so the letters are freely rearranged

parts.note: OK means so-so, middling or moderate

explanation.surface: Someone is going away shortly, along with an English Liberal and a moderate, as if leaving politics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liberal' and 'moderate' read as political labels: the first signals the anagram, the second means merely acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to go away or depart, an informal British phrase for leaving.

clue.text: Long to join club in film studios

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a wood is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: An aspiring actor yearning to sign up with a club at the movie studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinewood Studios in Buckinghamshire is a major British film studio, home of the Bond films.

clue.text: Wobbly blundering mile, I'm one of 4's

definitions.note: 4 is Norman Foster, so this means a structure he designed

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady, so the letters shake into a new order

explanation.surface: A footbridge complains that it wobbles, blundering along a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is also a nod to the subject: London's Millennium Bridge was nicknamed the Wobbly Bridge when it swayed on opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Foster designed the Thames footbridge between St Paul's and Tate Modern, opened in 2000.

clue.text: Rebels like to work, workers likely to strike?

definitions.note: worker bees that are aggressive and quick to sting

indicators.note: the letters are put to work, worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Militants enjoy labour, and employees look set to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action; here it means to sting. Worker bees are the colony's workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Africanised honeybees are notorious for attacking in swarms, so their workers are especially prone to sting.

clue.text: Basic issue recalled about stuff, including redundancy, primarily

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the rest
called back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: issue means offspring, a son

indicators.note: the filling word takes in the next letter

parts.note: to stuff is to fill

indicators.note: only the first letter of redundancy is used

explanation.surface: A cost-cutting memo about padding and redundancies, being fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no extras or embellishments is plain and basic, as in a budget airline.

clue.text: Fruit has gone off — lemon, too

indicators.note: fruit gone off is spoiled, so both words' letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fruit bowl in decline: something has rotted, and the lemon as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' works on gone and, with 'too', on lemon as well, giving OGEN and MELON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ogen is a small sweet variety of melon developed in Israel, so it is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Line drawn under this word of doubt over muse parting nicer lips

indicators.note: the pieces part, or separate, the two outer letters
the lips of a word are its outer letters
in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: um is a hesitant noise expressing uncertainty
Erato is the Muse of love poetry

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over a muse that makes pretty lips part, a line drawn under it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line drawn under this' reads as a conclusion; it is the bar beneath the top of a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: In a written fraction the top number sits above the dividing line, with the denominator below.

clue.text: See 11
Racket sport

definitions.meaning: a racket is a scheme or line of business
any sport, such as tennis or football, is a contest played for fun

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a scam or dodge is a racket, and a match or pastime is a sport.

clue.text: One of 4's in a pickle?

definitions.meaning: 4 is Norman Foster; 30 St Mary Axe in London is his tower nicknamed after a pickled cucumber
a small cucumber preserved in vinegar is found in a jar of pickles

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a pickle' suggests trouble, but here it is literal: the thing is in a pickle jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pickled cucumber shares its name with Foster's City of London skyscraper, 30 St Mary Axe.

clue.text: One of 4's, wife finally bagged by eligible bachelor?

indicators.note: taken inside, as if put in a bag

parts.note: an eligible bachelor is a desirable, often rich, catch

indicators.note: only the last letter of wife

parts.note: a stag is a man going to his own bachelor party

explanation.surface: A wife at last landed by a sought-after single man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eligible bachelor' reads as one stock phrase, but each word is clued separately: a wealthy man and a man on his last night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Foster rebuilt the German parliament building in Berlin in the 1990s, adding its glass dome.

clue.text: Laugh about blunder finally, short sharp sound

indicators.note: the laugh goes round the next letter

parts.note: a cackle is a loud raucous laugh

indicators.note: just the last letter of blunder

explanation.surface: Someone laughs at a gaffe at last, with a short sharp noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackle is a series of small snapping noises, like a fire or radio static.

clue.text: See 1
Composer not entirely a Creator

indicators.note: not all of the name, so its last letter goes

parts.note: Johannes Brahms, the German Romantic composer

explanation.surface: A composer who is not wholly a creative artist.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief the god of the Trimurti responsible for creating the universe.

clue.text: King into mindless chatter, as subordinate ruler

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the other letters
mindless chatter is senseless, so its letters lose their order

parts.note: R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king forced to sit through pointless small talk, as befits a lesser monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman Empire a tetrarch governed a quarter of a province under a higher authority, as Herod Antipas did.

clue.text: Sweet where OAP is in EastEnders, perhaps?

parts.words: where OAP is in EastEnders, perhaps
parts.note: EastEnders is an example of a soap, and in that word the letters OAP follow the S

explanation.surface: Asking where a pensioner character fits into the BBC soap opera EastEnders.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP suggests a pensioner in the long-running BBC soap; it is just letters, coming after S in SOAP.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the course after the main meal, pudding or dessert, is informally named this.

clue.text: See 27
Shocker by executioner confined to the walls of Sherlock's pad

indicators.note: the pieces are held within the letters that follow
the walls are the outside letters only
placed beside the other piece

parts.note: Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English hangman
boo is an exclamation meant to startle

explanation.surface: A grisly Holmes tale: a hangman's shock locked inside the detective's flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' suggests Sherlock's lodgings at Baker Street, but it is a drawing pad.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketchbook is a bound pad of drawing paper, so a pad is an informal synonym.

clue.text: See 9
French care for an English knight

parts.note: Norman describes someone from Normandy in France
to foster a child is to care for it

explanation.surface: A French nurse attending to an English knight.
explanation.definitionFit: The architect Lord Foster was knighted in 1990, so he is an English knight.

clue.text: Street cutting through centre, one with an obligation, is one of 4's

indicators.note: the abbreviation cuts into the middle of the other word

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre
an ower is someone who owes

explanation.surface: A road slicing through a town centre, past a debtor, is a landmark of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Foster designed the Manhattan skyscraper for the Hearst media corporation, finished in 2006.
